# Appeal of Denial – Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination, dated 2026-08-11
**Member:** Morgan Foster
**Member ID:** W276906709
**Reference Number:** POC-EED29F7594-68772
**Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), Kentucky
**Governing Policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), effective 2025-11-15 — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

Dear Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which was denied on 2026-08-11 with the stated reason that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Anthem to reconsider this decision.

**A note on the criteria cited in my file.** The medical policy referenced for my case is the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline (MSK02-1125.1). However, the specific criteria language that was provided to me in connection with this denial — for example, the language stating that "shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications," along with the sections on hemiarthroplasty and reverse shoulder arthroplasty — all describe criteria for **shoulder** procedures, not knee procedures. My request is for a partial **knee** replacement. I have not been given the knee-specific medical necessity criteria from this policy that would actually apply to my case, so I am not able to show point-by-point how my records meet policy language I have not been shown. I am asking Anthem to identify and apply the section of this policy that actually governs partial knee replacement, and to explain how that section's criteria were applied to my imaging and records.

**What my records show.** Regardless of which specific criteria apply, my medical records document the following, which I believe support the medical necessity of this surgery:

- I have had progressive knee pain for 14 months that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, from 2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-26 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI of my knee on 2026-06-27 showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially.
- I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain.
- On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

I am asking that Anthem review this information together with the correct, knee-specific criteria under the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline, and reverse the denial of CPT 27446.

**What I am requesting:**
1. A full reconsideration of this denial based on the complete clinical record described above.
2. Identification of the specific knee-replacement criteria under Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1) that were applied to my case, since the criteria referenced in my denial materials appear to address shoulder procedures rather than knee procedures.
3. A written response confirming the outcome of this appeal.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-07, and I am submitting it well before that deadline. I have been advised to send this appeal to the address listed on my denial letter, and I am also available by phone or through the Anthem member portal if additional information is needed.

Thank you for your time and attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Morgan Foster
Member ID: W276906709
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
